title: Your Cat Most Likely Can't Taste Sugar: 1 Broken Gene
description:
Can cats taste sugar? Most likely not. In mammals the sweet taste receptor is two proteins paired up, and in cats the gene for one of them (Tas1r2) is broken: a 2005 study found a 247-base pair piece of it missing. The other half works. The authors say cats most likely cannot detect sweet-tasting compounds and that the rest of a cat's sense of taste is normal. The same piece was missing in all six domestic cats tested and in the one tiger and the one cheetah tested. A 2023 paper by scientists at a pet food company (Mars Petcare) proposes that umami, the meaty taste, is a cat's main appetizing taste, and its authors guess this is part of why tuna is so palatable to cats. None of these papers says why a cat stares at dessert. Chocolate and the sweetener xylitol are on the ASPCA's list of people foods to avoid feeding pets: if you suspect your pet ate some, note the amount and contact your veterinarian or poison control.
